data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A redundant monolith is more resilient than a decentralized network when the primary failure mode is 'resource exhaustion' rather than 'logic bugs', as centralized capacity management is more efficient than fragmented buffers.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The failure is caused by a systemic software bug rather than load.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized network employs a robust, non-centralized load-shedding protocol.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Strictly more total internal redundancy allows for global load balancing and 'sacrificial' node shedding, whereas a decentralized network of small services lacks the aggregate buffer to absorb massive traffic spikes, leading to cascading failures.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
